guide.summary: Temples, a heritage opera house and Fort and Colaba galleries, with breakfast spots, dinners, bakeries and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Check closing days before you cross town: TARQ and Project 88 open Tuesday to Saturday, Masque serves dinner Tuesday to Sunday, and Sakshi Gallery, Gallery Chemould Prescott Road and American Express Bakery close on Sundays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: TARQ and Project 88 open Tuesday to Saturday, and Masque serves dinner Tuesday to Sunday. Sakshi Gallery, Gallery Chemould Prescott Road and American Express Bakery close on Sundays.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Masque takes an advance deposit to confirm every table, and Indian Accent asks Rs 1000 per guest, forfeited for cancellations under 24 hours or no-shows. Royal Opera House phone booking runs 10am to 5pm, Monday to Saturday.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins and queues
toolkit.copy: Indian Accent accommodates walk-ins when possible and holds booked tables for only 30 minutes. Swati Snacks in Tardeo takes last entry at 10pm, and the Global Vipassana Pagoda is free with no booking, open daily 9am to 7pm.

toolkit.label: Dress, age and bags
toolkit.copy: Masque admits guests 12 and over and Indian Accent children 10 and above, while Ziya asks gentlemen for full-length trousers and closed shoes. Shree Siddhivinayak Temple and the Global Vipassana Pagoda ask for modest dress, and the Pagoda bans outside food.

guide.dek: Plan galleries for Tuesday to Saturday, book tasting menus well ahead, and keep Sunday for temples, the Pagoda and hotel cafés.
intro: Fort and Colaba reward you with small galleries that publish their own hours. TARQ, in KK (Navsari) Chambers on AK Nayak Marg, opens Tuesday to Saturday from 11am to 6:30pm and lists Garima Gupta's Home-sick from 29 October to 19 December 2026. Project 88 on N.A. Sawant Road keeps Tuesday to Saturday hours, 11am to 7pm, and Sakshi Gallery on 3rd Pasta Lane opens 11am to 6pm, closing on Sundays and public holidays. Gallery Chemould Prescott Road, in Queens Mansion, opens Monday to Saturday, 10am to 6pm, and DAG lists Faces and Facets: Satyajit Ray in Colour as ongoing at its gallery inside The Taj Mahal Palace.

For landmarks, Shree Siddhivinayak Temple on S.K. Bole Marg in Prabhadevi publishes a full darshan schedule: on most days the last aarti is at 9:50pm, while Tuesday runs from early darshan at 3:15am to 11:30pm. The temple asks you to switch off your phone, avoid revealing dress and leave footwear at the stand. Haji Ali Dargah, set offshore off Lala Lajpatrai Marg, lists ziyarat timings of 5:30am to 10pm and says non-Muslims may visit. Further north at Gorai, the Global Vipassana Pagoda opens daily from 9am to 7pm with no entry fee, no outside food and a dress code covering knees and shoulders.

Meals range from Swati Snacks in Tardeo, which opens at 11:45am with last entry at 10pm, to Burma Burma in Kothari House near Kala Ghoda, serving lunch and dinner in two windows. For a big night, Masque in Mahalaxmi serves a 10-course tasting menu, priced at Rs 9999 from 1 October 2026, at dinner Tuesday to Sunday from 7pm; it needs a deposit and admits guests 12 and over. Indian Accent at Jio World Centre opens seven days and asks Rs 1000 per guest to confirm. At ITC Maratha in Andheri East, Avartana serves dinner from 7pm and lunch on Sundays only, with smart casuals and formal footwear expected.

The Oberoi at Nariman Point can carry a whole day: Fenix opens at 6:30am, The Champagne Lounge serves single-origin coffee from 8am, The Oberoi Patisserie & Delicatessen sells breads and pastries from 10am to 8pm, and The Eau Bar pours from 5pm to 1:30am with a DJ on Saturday and Sunday. Ziya there asks gentlemen to wear full-length trousers and closed shoes. In Bandra, American Express Bakery on Hill Road opens Monday to Saturday from 9am, and Hakkasan on Waterfield Road serves dinner until 1am. For an evening show, the Royal Opera House lists performances into November 2026 and forbids filming or recording during performances.
summaryCards: Pair Shree Siddhivinayak Temple in Prabhadevi with Haji Ali Dargah, then spend a Tuesday to Saturday afternoon in Fort and Colaba, when TARQ and Project 88 are both open.
Start with breakfast at Fenix from 6:30am or single-origin coffee at The Champagne Lounge from 8am, then pick up pastries at The Oberoi Patisserie & Delicatessen from 10am.
Masque needs a deposit and serves dinner Tuesday to Sunday, Indian Accent asks Rs 1000 per guest, and Sakshi Gallery, Gallery Chemould Prescott Road and American Express Bakery close on Sundays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The input lists were almost entirely generic, so every confirmed place was added as a gap candidate. Several major sites could not be read: CSMVS (no readable content), Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum (access denied), NMACC (reCAPTCHA), The Taj Mahal Palace and Four Seasons outlets (HTTP 403), and The Bombay Canteen, Subko, Blue Tokai and Bombay Sweet Shop (HTTP 429). NCPA publishes a current events calendar but no postal address on the pages read, and the Nehru Planetarium page carries an ambiguous 'remains closed in the year 2026' notice, so both were left out. Jehangir Art Gallery and DAG publish no opening hours; Jehangir shows two slightly different addresses. Oberoi outlets give only 'Nariman Point, Mumbai 400021' as the address, Peshawri lists 'Lunch & Dinner' without times, and several hotel and restaurant listings rely on hours notices rather than dated 2026 content. Haji Ali Dargah gives a location description rather than a postal address.
injectionLikeTextIgnored: theobroma.in homepage: a 'Summarise Theobroma with AI' section ('Menu, bestsellers, offers and nearest store in one answer.') with buttons that open ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI with a prefilled 'Summarize this page' query. A sharing feature, not acted on.
